Definition: an inclosure, i.e. cage (for an animal)
BiblicalUsage: The cage is where the lion is put, and Ezekiel says the nations took the young lion in chains and brought him to Babylon in a cage. The word appears once, in the lament for the princes of Israel. The cage is the end of a king who roared and devoured.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cage shows what happens to princes who devour their people: the nations cage them, and the roaring stops.
